projects.name: Svara
projects.description: A Windows dictation app that turns speech into text at the active cursor. I built the local speech pipeline, application-aware text insertion, recovery behavior, and desktop release workflow.
projects.summary: A Windows dictation app that turns speech into text at the active cursor. I built the local speech pipeline, application-aware text insertion, recovery behavior, and desktop release workflow.

details.title: The problem
details.body: Dictation needs to work inside the tools people already use. Transcription accuracy alone is not enough: clipped first words, lost recordings, duplicate text, or an accidental Enter in a terminal can make the tool unusable.

details.title: What I built
bullets: Connected microphone capture, a pre-roll audio buffer, local speech recognition, transcript cleanup, and text insertion into a system-wide Windows workflow.
Added streaming transcription, configurable CPU/CUDA inference, personal vocabulary, local history, and optional LLM cleanup.
Built tray controls, recording feedback, settings, packaged releases, and an update flow that waits for the user to restart.

details.title: Engineering decisions
bullets: Kept speech recognition on the device, with CPU support so the app does not require a dedicated GPU.
Made insertion aware of the target application: terminal-safe text handling, editor-specific paste behavior, and a clipboard fallback when Windows privilege boundaries block input.
Used temporary local recovery audio to protect unfinished dictation and removed transcript content from ordinary diagnostic logs. Optional cleanup depends on the configured model endpoint.

details.title: Evidence and current status
details.body: Released as an open-source Windows application. Recent commits repair recording lifecycle behavior and engine selection; the repository includes regression tests for cleanup, insertion, configuration, and log redaction. Its benchmark harness measures latency and transcription quality on the user’s hardware. Performance varies by model and device; this case study does not claim a universal speed or accuracy score.

projects.name: Dreamer
projects.description: An idea workspace with durable AI research and planning workflows. I built a system where agents propose reviewable document changes, retain their evidence, and recover interrupted work.
projects.summary: An idea workspace with durable AI research and planning workflows. I built a system where agents propose reviewable document changes, retain their evidence, and recover interrupted work.

details.title: The problem
details.body: An interesting idea can disappear into a notes app, while a long AI conversation is difficult to audit or resume. I wanted research, planning, and critique to produce a durable document that the owner can review and improve.

details.title: What I built
bullets: Developed the idea vault, API, web and mobile clients, and a shared worker system for research, planning, critique, and refinement.
Represented agent edits as attributed section proposals with version history, keeping the owner in control of the working document.
Added an opt-in discovery workflow that investigates ideas, records supporting and opposing evidence, and applies explicit acceptance rules.

details.title: Engineering decisions
bullets: Used PostgreSQL-backed work records, worker leases, heartbeats, retry policies, and idempotent scheduling to make long-running work recoverable.
Separated provider routing and usage accounting from the workflow so model changes do not require rebuilding the orchestration layer.
Added evidence checks and publication quarantine so a model’s recommendation cannot by itself establish commercial viability.

details.title: Evidence and current status
details.body: A private personal project running locally. The source includes unit and database integration tests for document proposals, worker behavior, migrations, and recovery. Local release records document container builds and a database restore drill. Managed staging, broader live-provider checks, and signed mobile-device acceptance remain before a public release. Generated ideas and model scores are not evidence of customers or revenue.

projects.name: Deep Researcher
projects.description: An evidence-first research engine that turns a question into a report with traceable claims. I built planning, retrieval, source extraction, claim verification, and resumable execution behind an API and browser dashboard.
projects.summary: An evidence-first research engine that turns a question into a report with traceable claims. I built planning, retrieval, source extraction, claim verification, and resumable execution behind an API and browser dashboard.

details.title: The problem
details.body: A report can look well cited while its sources fail to support the actual claims. The engineering challenge was to preserve evidence throughout research and prevent unsupported material from reaching the final report.

details.title: What I built
bullets: Implemented a planner with bounded specialist workstreams, iterative searches, full-page and PDF extraction, and an adversarial review of missing or contradictory evidence.
Built a claim ledger containing source references, quoted passages, document locations, and provenance hashes.
Added SQLite checkpoints, cancellation and restart, live progress events, a REST API, a dashboard, and a command-line interface.

details.title: Engineering decisions
bullets: Separated exact-quote matching from model-based entailment checks: a quote must exist in the retrieved text, and the claim must be supported by that quote in context.
Selected passages relevant to each question instead of always truncating documents at the beginning.
Made the pipeline stop when evidence gates fail, while preserving diagnostics and rejected evidence for inspection. Search and model providers remain replaceable.

details.title: Evidence and current status
details.body: A working local research prototype with private source. Tests exercise persisted evidence, fabricated-quote rejection, document passage selection, URL boundaries, and PDF extraction using controlled fixtures and mocked services. Those tests verify pipeline behavior; they do not establish real-world factual accuracy or superiority to other research products. Live research still needs source review.

projects.name: JustHireMe iOS
projects.description: A native mobile edition of my job-search workspace. I built SwiftUI flows and a separate account-scoped cloud API, with explicit boundaries between the mobile experience and the existing desktop product.
projects.summary: A native mobile edition of my job-search workspace. I built SwiftUI flows and a separate account-scoped cloud API, with explicit boundaries between the mobile experience and the existing desktop product.

details.title: The problem
details.body: The desktop app stores career data on one machine. A mobile edition needs authenticated accounts, secure sessions, purchase recovery, and a backend designed for multiple users. Reusing a local desktop API directly would cross the wrong trust boundary.

details.title: What I built
bullets: Implemented email-code sign-in, profile editing, saved opportunities, application status tracking, reviewable drafts, sharing, account export, and deletion.
Built native subscription and credit flows with StoreKit and server-side purchase recording, plus recovery of unfinished transactions.
Created a clearly labelled demo with fictional data so the interface can be explored without an account, payments, or AI requests.

details.title: Engineering decisions
bullets: Kept the mobile cloud service separate from the desktop sidecar and scoped account content through authenticated endpoints.
Stored session credentials in the iOS Keychain and kept account content in memory with an ephemeral networking session.
Made purchase completion depend on server acknowledgement. Mobile drafting uses explicit user inputs; desktop discovery and graph/vector matching are not advertised as mobile features.

details.title: Evidence and current status
details.body: Private source; in development. A successful hosted iPhone simulator run verifies native compilation and demo unit/UI tests, including onboarding, tracking, dark mode, and larger text. Real authentication, AI and payment integration, physical-device testing, signing, and TestFlight/App Store release remain separate milestones. This is not yet a released iOS app.

projects.name: Ori no Michi
projects.description: An interactive origami learning experience with a custom paper-folding engine. I combined geometry, 3D animation, authored lessons, and narrated tutorials to make each fold understandable.
projects.summary: An interactive origami learning experience with a custom paper-folding engine. I combined geometry, 3D animation, authored lessons, and narrated tutorials to make each fold understandable.

details.title: The problem
details.body: A static diagram often hides which layer moves, where it should land, and why a fold matters. I wanted learners to inspect a step from different angles, replay it, and pause while following along with real paper.

details.title: What I built
bullets: Implemented rigid polygon clipping and folding, layer selection, mountain/valley motion, unfolding, and turn-over steps.
Connected the engine to interactive lessons with crease guides, moving-flap highlights, alignment targets, orbit controls, and geometry-derived previews.
Built a tutorial theater with sequenced camera motion, chapters, scrubbing, captions, narration, playback speed, and a fold-along pause mode.

details.title: Engineering decisions
bullets: Selected moving layers using the authored crease segment so a fold on one flap does not move unrelated paper across the model.
Generated previews from the same geometry as the lesson to keep the visual explanation consistent with playback.
Used separate schematic checkpoints for complex workshops and provided reduced-motion behavior, keyboard controls, and device-local progress.

details.title: Evidence and current status
details.body: A private personal learning app. The source includes tests for paper-area conservation, finite coordinates, rigid edge lengths, layer selection, and tutorial chapter coverage. It also contains original narrated lesson films and caption files. The engine models rigid folds; it is not a general paper-physics or collision simulator, and complex workshop diagrams intentionally simplify hidden layers.

projects.name: LearnAI
projects.description: An applied-AI learning handbook with interactive exercises and companion audio/video lessons. I built multiple ways to explore the same concepts, from reading an explanation to experimenting with a simplified model.
projects.summary: An applied-AI learning handbook with interactive exercises and companion audio/video lessons. I built multiple ways to explore the same concepts, from reading an explanation to experimenting with a simplified model.

details.title: The problem
details.body: Developers moving into applied AI need to connect familiar software-engineering skills to new concepts such as embeddings, retrieval, tool use, and evaluation. A list of definitions does not show how those ideas behave.

details.title: What I built
bullets: Created a standalone documentation site with topic navigation, an in-page contents list, themes, and progress tracking.
Built interactive exercises for token sampling, embedding space, retrieval pipelines, prompt-injection awareness, agent failures, and model-based evaluation.
Added quizzes and interview practice, plus companion audio/video players with transcripts, episode navigation, playback controls, and saved progress.

details.title: Engineering decisions
bullets: Kept the handbook and playground in plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript so they can run without a build pipeline or application server.
Used browser storage for learning progress and media position, supporting short sessions across reading, watching, and listening.
Used simplified interactive demonstrations to expose cause and effect. They teach concepts; they are not production tokenizers, retrieval engines, or model benchmarks.

details.title: Evidence and current status
details.body: Private personal educational project. The repository contains the handbook, working playground code, media players, and companion lesson assets. Source review confirms the interactive exercises and local progress storage. It has not been evaluated as a formal course, and no learner-outcome or adoption claims are made.

projects.name: EstimateIO
projects.description: A browser game for developing an intuition for physical scale. I built direct manipulation, consistent measurement rules, and visual feedback that explains how a guess compares with the answer.
projects.summary: A browser game for developing an intuition for physical scale. I built direct manipulation, consistent measurement rules, and visual feedback that explains how a guess compares with the answer.

details.title: The problem
details.body: Numbers alone make it difficult to judge size. I wanted players to learn by resizing an object beside a familiar reference, constructing a length, or placing an object on a scale.

details.title: What I built
bullets: Implemented three game modes: relative size comparison, making a measurement, and placement on a logarithmic size line.
Built pinch and drag controls with keyboard and button alternatives, unit selection, hints, streaks, and local best scores.
Made answer reveals overlay the guess and correct silhouette at a shared baseline so the error is visually understandable.

details.title: Engineering decisions
bullets: Stored canonical measurements in centimetres with explicit unit conversion and reference dimensions.
Scored proportional error symmetrically: guessing half the size and twice the size receives the same score.
Handled pointer addition, release, cancellation, and near-coincident fingers without sudden jumps or invalid scale values. Rotating challenge sets keep short runs varied.

details.title: Evidence and current status
details.body: A local personal browser game with private source. Logic tests cover score symmetry, conversions, logarithmic mapping, challenge rotation, and gesture transitions. References are attached to measurements; artwork is stylized and screen pixels do not represent life-size units. Its optional browser-tool integration is experimental and was not verified in a browser supporting that API.

projects.name: Socratis
projects.description: Voice AI Agent-powered technical interview platform with real-time voice interaction, live code feedback, and intelligent assessment using LiveKit, Deepgram, and Groq.
projects.summary: Real-time AI interviewer that runs live coding interviews over WebRTC voice. Candidates code in Monaco while a Python agent watches every keystroke via chat-context injection, asks Socratic hints only when needed, and writes a forensic post-interview report.
highlights: Real-time code awareness — agent sees every edit via chat-context injection
Socratic method — only speaks when detecting bugs, approach changes or stalls
Forensic report with exact-quote communication analysis and hallucination cross-checks

details.title: The setup
details.body: Candidate codes in Monaco. A Python voice agent drives the interview over WebRTC with LiveKit for transport, Deepgram for STT and aura-helios TTS, and Silero for voice-activity detection. The model is Groq's Llama-3.3 70B. Frontend is Next.js 14; an Express + MongoDB backend holds sessions.

details.title: Real-time code awareness
details.body: Earlier versions hallucinated about the candidate's code. V3's fix was Chat Context Injection: every edit in the Monaco editor pushes an explicit system message into the agent's context, so the model literally sees every diff instead of guessing.

details.title: Behavior rules
bullets: Socratic — hint, don't solve
Speaks only when detecting bugs, approach changes or stalls
Adapts to any coding problem; asks for a description when missing
Cross-references verbal claims against the code to catch overclaims

details.title: Post-interview forensics
details.body: The same agent runs a second pass after the call ends. Strict Big-O on time and space. Line-by-line bug fixes in "Line X: [Issue] → [Fix]" format. Communication analysis citing exact transcript quotes. A hallucination check cross-references the candidate's claims against their actual code. Output renders on a radar-chart result page.

projects.name: Waldo
projects.description: A multimodal RAG prototype for question answering over PDFs containing text, tables, and figures.
projects.summary: A multimodal RAG prototype that ingests PDF text, tables, and figures. A LangGraph workflow routes, grades, and rewrites retrieval queries, while vision-model captions make figures searchable.
highlights: Multimodal ingestion — text + tables + figures in a single pipeline
LangGraph agent with query rewriting, relevance grading and retry logic
Relevance checks and refusal handling for unsupported questions

details.title: The problem
details.body: Most RAG systems only handle text. Waldo is built for real-world docs where the answer might live in a table, bar chart or figure caption — research papers, medical reports, technical spec sheets.

details.title: Ingestion pipeline
bullets: IBM Docling extracts document structure with high fidelity
RapidOCR falls back for scanned pages
Gemini VLM transcribes figures to searchable semantic text
Sentence Transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) embed chunks into Qdrant

details.title: Agentic retrieval
bullets: LangGraph routes between direct response and retrieval
Every retrieved doc gets LLM-graded for relevance
Failed queries are rewritten (max 2 retries)
Visual-query detection auto-includes figure transcriptions
Groq serves the final generation for low latency

details.title: Guardrails
details.body: Relevance checks and refusal instructions aim to keep answers grounded in the document. When vision-model quota is unavailable, ingestion can fall back to extracted captions. These controls reduce failure modes but cannot guarantee hallucination-free answers.

details.title: Current scope
details.body: An assessment prototype with in-memory retrieval and a single-document workflow. It demonstrates multimodal ingestion and retrieval orchestration; production persistence, multi-user isolation, and operational evaluation are outside this version.

projects.name: SSS
projects.description: Screen Shot Sorter
projects.summary: Local AI-powered screenshot organizer. Qwen2-VL-2B runs on your GPU, classifying images into nine semantic buckets, extracting URLs, cleaning text and generating per-image markdown logs.
highlights: Fully local inference — no cloud API calls
Qwen2-VL vision pipeline + URL extraction + text cleaning
GPU-memory managed: cache clear every 5 images, bfloat16 weights

details.title: The problem
details.body: 4,000-file screenshot folders with zero structure. Manual sorting is unrealistic.

details.title: Pipeline
bullets: Vision model (Qwen2-VL-2B via Transformers/PyTorch) ingests each image → structured understanding
Classifier routes to one of nine categories — anime, tech, hiring, finance, learning, health, news, memes, misc
Link extractor pulls every URL in the image
Text cleaner strips hashtags, emojis, formatting noise
Per-image .txt log in `./output/extracted/` + master `links.md` index

details.title: Performance tuning
bullets: Model loads once at startup, images process one at a time
GPU cache clears every 5 images
Uses `bfloat16` for reduced VRAM footprint
~5–10 sec per image on RTX 4060 (8 GB VRAM target)
No cloud API calls — fully local inference

projects.name: DryRunVisualised
projects.summary: Real-time algorithm visualizer that renders data-structure operations in both 2D (SVG) and 3D (WebGL via Three.js). Write Python or C++ in Monaco, hit Run, watch each line execute with full variable inspection.
highlights: Dual 2D / 3D view toggle with draggable nodes in the 3D scene
50+ pre-built algorithms across searching, sorting, graphs, DP, backtracking
Per-line trace replay with step forward/backward and speed slider

details.title: What it does
details.body: Write an algorithm, step through its execution, and watch arrays sort, graphs traverse, linked lists re-wire and matrices transform — step by step, with every variable's current state rendered live. Toggle between an interactive 2D view (SVG/DOM) and an immersive 3D scene (Three.js + React Three Fiber) with orbit controls and draggable nodes.

details.title: Execution pipeline
bullets: Python runs client-side in Pyodide (WebAssembly)
C++ compiles remotely via Godbolt Compiler Explorer API (GCC 14.1)
Instrumentation injects `sys.settrace` (Python) and stderr macros (C++)
Each line emits a JSON snapshot: `{ line, stack, heap, stdout }`
`vizDetector.ts` classifies variables (array/grid/graph/linked-list/tree/scalar) and routes them

details.title: Experience details
bullets: 50+ pre-built algorithms across searching, sorting, graphs, DP, backtracking
Resizable panels — editor, variables, visualization
Amber glow on modified cells, strikethrough on previous values
Force-directed graph layouts for adjacency-list graphs
SVG linked-list nodes with data | next compartments and curved arrow connectors

projects.name: A18-INFINION-
projects.summary: Multi-agent static bug detector for specialized C++ (Infineon RDI API). A central Orchestrator dispatches Code Parser, MCP Lookup, Bug Detector and Bug Describer agents through a two-layer detection strategy that boosts confidence when pattern matching and LLM reasoning agree.
highlights: Context-first — pulls API docs via MCP before inspecting the code
Two-layer detection (pattern + LLM) with consensus-based confidence
Multi-bug support, per-snippet isolation, CSV in / CSV out

details.title: The task
details.body: Generic linters miss domain-specific mistakes in specialized C++ because they don't know the API's rules. The Infineon A18 Challenge was to build a reviewer that does.

details.title: Context-first design
details.body: Before any LLM sees the code, the MCP Lookup Agent queries an MCP server (FastMCP + BGE embeddings) against the RDI API documentation and pulls the relevant rules. Only then does the Bug Detector run — with the API manual already in context.

details.title: Pipeline
bullets: Orchestrator dispatches agents per snippet
Code Parser classifies each line (code/comment/preprocessor) + 1-indexed numbering
MCP Lookup queries the docs server with caching
Bug Detector runs pattern-match + LLM-reasoning layers; boosts confidence on consensus
Bug Describer produces human-readable explanations citing the manual

details.title: Multi-provider
details.body: Gemini 2.0, DeepSeek V3 and GPT-4o are interchangeable. Detections below 70% confidence are dropped. CSV in → CSV out for batch evaluation.

projects.name: Portfolio-cool
projects.summary: This portfolio site. Vite + React + TypeScript with Tailwind and Framer Motion. Radial theme toggle, context-aware custom cursor with paint trails, magnetic buttons, live GitHub stats.
highlights: Radial theme transition tied to click coordinates
Custom cursor with contrast-aware color + paint trails
Sticky-hero stacked-section scroll pattern powered by Lenis

details.title: Signature interactions
bullets: Radial theme transition — click-coordinate-anchored circle expansion
Custom cursor with contrast-aware color + paint trails + eater bot
Magnetic buttons that pull toward the cursor
Film-grain SVG overlay at 3% opacity for analog texture
Sticky-hero stacked-section scroll pattern via Lenis

details.title: Live data
bullets: Stars via Cloudflare Workers counter (bypasses GitHub rate limits)
Commits via the jogruber contributions proxy
PRs via GitHub's search endpoint

details.title: Build
details.body: Lazy-loaded sections via React.lazy + Suspense. TypeScript strict mode throughout. 100dvh mobile layouts, AA-contrast foreground colors. Deployed to Vercel.

projects.name: RupeeRoast
projects.description: The AI-powered financial forensic tool that turns messy bank PDFs into actionable insights—and roasts your spending habits
projects.summary: AI financial forensic tool that parses messy Indian bank PDFs (including UPI), categorizes every transaction via an LLM, and produces both a dashboard and a Groq-powered 'Indian Dad / Gen-Z' roast of your impulsive purchases.
highlights: Universal PDF extraction for messy bank statements incl. UPI transactions
Roaster persona critiques impulsive spending with data-backed sass
Interactive charts: category breakdowns, monthly trends, impulsive vs necessary

details.title: What it does
details.body: Hand it a bank statement PDF (Kotak, HDFC, SBI, whatever). It extracts every transaction including UPI, classifies into categories, and produces two artifacts: an interactive dashboard and a roast of your impulsive spending.

details.title: Extraction
bullets: PyMuPDF4LLM as the primary parser — much better than plain PyPDF for complex layouts
PyPDF as fallback for edge cases
Pydantic-validated schemas throughout

details.title: AI layer
bullets: Groq Llama-3 for fast categorization
Gemini generates the 'Indian Dad / Gen-Z' persona roast

details.title: Frontend
details.body: Next.js 15 App Router + React 19 + Tailwind 4 + Framer Motion. Recharts for the dashboard, Plotly for the complex interactive views. The featured chart is impulsive-vs-necessary. One `python run_delulu.py` boots both services.

projects.name: EmailDrafter
projects.description: AI-assisted email drafting app with a Python backend and a modern React + Vite + Tailwind frontend.
projects.summary: AI-assisted email drafting app — FastAPI backend, React + Vite + Tailwind frontend. Users enter context and tone/length preferences; the backend calls an LLM to draft or refine; the UI shows live previews.
highlights: Separate /draft and /refine endpoints with prompt-level control
Hot-reload dev loop via Vite + uvicorn --reload
Swappable backend — frontend only talks to a thin api.js wrapper

details.title: What it does
details.body: Two modes: draft from scratch (prompt + optional tone/length hints) and refine (existing draft + instructions). Live preview in the UI before you copy or send.

details.title: API surface
bullets: POST /api/draft — { prompt, tone?, length? } → { draft }
POST /api/refine — { draft, instructions } → { draft }

details.title: Architecture
details.body: Monorepo with `backend/` (Python + venv + requirements.txt) and `frontend/my-app/` (Vite). All API calls funneled through `src/api.js` so the base URL is environment-swappable. Hot reload on both sides.

projects.name: Korosuke
projects.description: A personal AI sidebar assistant built with PyQt5 and Ollama. It provides a sliding sidebar interface, chat-like conversation, and lightweight integration with LLaMA models.
projects.summary: PyQt5 sliding-sidebar desktop assistant. Chat with a local LLaMA via Ollama, toggle with a hotkey, runs inference on a background thread so the UI never blocks.
highlights: Sliding sidebar UI with non-blocking background worker
Local Ollama inference — no cloud round-trips
ESC to hide, re-run to toggle behavior

details.title: What it does
details.body: A sidebar that slides in from the screen edge for AI chat, and slides away when dismissed. All inference runs against local Ollama (default `llama3.2:1b`) so it works offline with zero API keys.

details.title: Details
bullets: PyQt5 with smooth slide animations and styled chat bubbles
Background QThread worker — UI never freezes during generation
PID-based hotkey toggle: re-running the script flips visibility
ESC hides the sidebar

projects.name: ASCIIRealTime
projects.description: Real Time ASCII video streaming using user camera
projects.summary: Browser demo that turns your webcam feed into real-time ASCII or emoji art. Optional MediaPipe Selfie Segmentation masks the background. Zero build — vanilla JS + Tailwind via CDN.
highlights: ASCII text mode + emoji-canvas mode with per-glyph caching
MediaPipe Selfie Segmentation for optional background removal
Privacy — all processing in-browser, video never leaves your device

details.title: How it works
bullets: Samples camera frames to an offscreen canvas at a dynamic grid size
Per-cell luminance via perceptual luma: `0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B`
Maps brightness → character from active palette (light → dark)
Image smoothing disabled everywhere for pixel-crisp edges

details.title: Modes
bullets: ASCII text — `<pre>` with dynamically-sized font
Emoji — `<canvas>` grid with per-glyph bitmap caching for alignment
Palettes: Basic, Extended, Blocks, Emoji, Custom

details.title: Privacy
details.body: All processing in-browser. Video never leaves the device. External libraries load from CDNs.

projects.name: Health-os
projects.summary: Mobile-first PWA dashboard for workouts and meals. Next.js 14 App Router with a viewport-locked layout where only internal panes scroll — the page itself never grows a scrollbar.
highlights: Installable PWA with offline-ready service worker
Viewport-locked (100dvh) layout with internal scroll panes only
Mobile-first responsive design

details.title: What it is
details.body: A progressive web app. Add to home screen on mobile and it runs like a native app. Service worker is only generated in production build (next-pwa is disabled in dev by design).

details.title: The layout trick
details.body: Whole page is locked to `h-[100dvh]` with `overflow-hidden` on the outer body. Only the workout list and meal list scroll internally. On mobile, `100dvh` handles the browser chrome properly so the app uses the full available screen at all times.

details.title: Stack
bullets: Next.js 14 App Router
TypeScript
Tailwind
next-pwa for the service worker generation

projects.name: GitArt
projects.summary: Browser-based tool that lets you paint your GitHub contribution graph like a canvas. Design a 52x7 heatmap, the app builds a real Git repository — in-browser via isomorphic-git on memfs, zipped with JSZip — whose commit timestamps reproduce that design when pushed.
highlights: Runs entirely in-browser — no server, no GitHub API, no fake identities
30+ built-in templates (Pac-Man, QR code, Christmas tree, Nyan trail...)
Image drop-in with 5-band quantization + text-to-pixels bitmap font

details.title: The concept
details.body: GitHub's profile page renders your commit activity as a 52-week x 7-day heatmap. GitArt treats that grid as a painter's canvas: pick colors, draw a design, and the app builds a real Git repo whose commit timestamps reproduce the design when pushed to a fresh empty repo.

details.title: Everything runs in the browser
bullets: isomorphic-git on a memfs virtual filesystem
JSZip packages .git/ + files into a single zip
No server writes, no GitHub API calls, no fake identities

details.title: Intensity mapping
details.body: Cells have intensity 0-4 mapping to 0 / 1 / 5 / 10 / 20 commits per day. The brightest cell (20 commits) stays within GitHub's "active user" bucket so the graph looks dramatic without looking synthetic.

details.title: Design tools
bullets: Brush (levels 0-4) + eraser
Drop-in images quantized to 5 intensity bands
Text-to-pixels via bitmap font
30+ templates — Pac-Man Chase, QR Code, Matrix Rain, Nyan Trail, Christmas Tree, Fireworks...
Time Machine — target any year 2022-2027, anchors to the first Sunday of that year

projects.name: GhostSync
projects.description: Control Antigravity IDE remotely via Telegram - from anywhere in the world.
projects.summary: Windows app that exposes Antigravity IDE to a private Telegram bot over a Cloudflare Tunnel, so you can trigger AI prompts and receive live IDE screenshots from anywhere — with a strict user whitelist and rate limiting.
highlights: Auto-generated Cloudflare tunnel — no port-forwarding required
Live IDE screenshots streamed back over Telegram
User-ID whitelist, rate limits, auto-deleted screenshots

details.title: What it does
details.body: Run Antigravity on your PC, configure GhostSync with your Telegram bot token and user ID, click Connect. From any Telegram client you can now send a folder path to open, fire AI prompts, and receive live screenshots of your IDE.

details.title: How the bridge works
bullets: Auto-downloads `cloudflared.exe` and spawns a Cloudflare Tunnel
python-telegram-bot listens for authorized commands
PyAutoGUI automates IDE input (window detection via %LOCALAPPDATA%)
CustomTkinter GUI; single PyInstaller .exe for non-Python users

details.title: Security
bullets: User-ID whitelist — only your Telegram account can issue commands
10 req/min rate limit
Screenshots auto-deleted after sending
Logs sanitize sensitive data
Credentials in %USERPROFILE%\.ghostsync\.env — never uploaded

projects.name: Kyoka
projects.description: Kyoka: Elite behavioral intelligence unit that transforms raw OSINT into deep psychological dossiers and actionable negotiation strategies using multi-agent AI.
projects.summary: OSINT-driven behavioral intelligence app. A tri-agent LangChain pipeline reads a target's digital footprint, synthesizes DISC and Big-Five traits, then produces actionable 'Battle Cards' with DOs, DON'Ts and opening lines.
highlights: Tri-agent pipeline: researcher → analyst → tactician
DISC + Big-Five + ego-hook detection from LinkedIn / GitHub / Twitter content
Luxury-tool UI with radar charts, magnetic hovers, chat simulator

details.title: The premise
details.body: In most high-stakes meetings you know someone's title but not their core drivers, shadow traits or preferred communication protocol. Kyoka closes that gap.

details.title: Tri-agent pipeline
bullets: Deep Diver (Tavily Search) — OSINT across LinkedIn, GitHub, X, YouTube
PsychProfiler (DeepSeek-V3 / Gemini) — DISC, Big-Five, archetypes, ego hooks
Strategist (GPT-4o / Gemini) — Battle Card with DOs, DON'Ts, opening lines

details.title: Backend
details.body: FastAPI + LangChain. A unified `run.py` creates the venv, installs both Python and Node deps, and launches backend + frontend in parallel.

details.title: Frontend
details.body: "Charcoal & Gold" luxury-concierge aesthetic — Playfair Display for headings, Inter for data. Radar charts visualize personality skew. Reveal cards, magnetic hovers, and a chat simulator let you rehearse the conversation before it happens.

projects.name: BranchGPT-Extension
projects.summary: Chrome extension that turns ChatGPT into a DAG-based chat tool. Fork any message into a parallel branch, visualize the tree in a side panel, and keep context clean. All data stored locally via IndexedDB.
highlights: True branching — fork any message into a parallel reality
Conversation tree rendered in a sleek side panel
Local-only IndexedDB storage; injects directly into the ChatGPT UI

React + TypeScript + Tailwind
Dexie.js over IndexedDB for local storage

projects.name: Forge
projects.description: A SOTA SDLC skill set for Claude Code — 16 lifecycle skills, a continuous-learning memory layer, and a live code-dependency graph.
projects.summary: One cohesive Claude Code plugin: 16 hand-off-linked SDLC skills (understand → brainstorm → architect → plan → tdd → debug → review → verify → ship), each encoding a falsifiable engineering rule — plus a local memory layer that learns from your sessions and a live, self-updating map of your codebase.
highlights: 16 namespaced lifecycle skills wired into one hand-off chain — discipline as falsifiable rules, not vibes
Two-tier continuous-learning memory: per-project instincts + anonymized global lessons, distilled from your own sessions
Live code-dependency graph (god-nodes, modules, blast-radius, cycles) patched incrementally so it never goes stale

details.title: The problem
details.body: Power users of Claude Code accumulate a dozen overlapping skill packs, and a raw model has predictable failure modes: it assumes silently, over-builds, edits code it doesn't understand, and claims success it never verified. Forge is one namespaced lifecycle that enforces engineering discipline AND learns from your sessions so the agent stops repeating mistakes.

details.title: Falsifiable, not aspirational
bullets: tdd: no production code without a failing test first — watch it fail, delete pre-test code
debug: after 3 failed fixes, question the architecture
verify: a claim → required-proof table before 'done' is allowed
Each skill names the rationalization it forbids, so the agent can't talk itself out of the process

details.title: The memory loop
details.body: Four lifecycle hooks feed a zero-dependency Node core: every Edit/Write/Bash is logged as compact JSONL, a throttled background distiller (Haiku) extracts trigger → action lessons through a strict quality gate, and the highest-confidence lessons are injected at session start. Its memory subsystem was later extracted into a second standalone plugin, engram.

details.title: The code graph
details.body: forge:graph builds a static import graph for JS/TS, Python, C/C++, Ruby and Rust (including tsconfig aliases), surfaces god-nodes, cycles and dead files, and is rebuilt once then patched by an mtime-diff on every stop — a high-accuracy skeleton that stays cheap.

Admin-approval workflow — only validated answers reach production

details.title: The problem

projects.name: Arohan
projects.description: The AI IPO Observatory — a research-grounded predictive model for the 2026 frontier-AI mega-IPOs.
projects.summary: An investor-research observatory for the 2026 AI mega-IPO window (OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI/SPCX): a probability-weighted comparables + scenario model rendered as P10–P90 fan charts, an expected-return heatmap, and an in-app reader for the full research corpus — built in a single day.
highlights: Four-layer scenario model: historical-comparables regression, fundamentals, demand overlay, macro gate
Fan-chart forecast lab with a live macro-stress slider and bear/base/bull toggles
8 markdown dossiers (~4,300 words, 24 sources) bundled and readable in-app

details.title: The model
details.body: A log-linear regression anchor fit on a 20-listing historical IPO dataset (1995–2025), a company-fundamentals layer from verified June 2026 marks, a demand-side overlay, and a macro gate. Nine scenario cells per company collapse into probability-weighted P10/P50/P90 bands, computed offline and embedded as static data.

details.title: Honest framing
details.body: An OpenAI listing at ~$1T would be ~6x the largest IPO in history, so the comparables regression is an anchor, not statistics-grade inference — every band is labelled probability-weighted, with wide error bars and caveats baked into each research file. A research exercise, not investment advice.

projects.name: NyaySaathi
projects.description: AI legal research assistant for Indian law — RAG over the Constitution, IT Act and FIRs with citation-backed answers.
projects.summary: AI legal assistant that gives Indian citizens accurate, citation-backed answers grounded strictly in verified statutes — a local Qdrant RAG with legal-aware chunking, reference-aware reranking, and support for ~13 Indian languages including romanized Hinglish.
highlights: Legal-aware chunking that preserves Article/Section/Part/Chapter structure
Hybrid retrieval + reranking with a Constitution-to-statute cross-link map
Refuses to hallucinate: context-only answers with official-source fallback

details.title: The problem
details.body: Statutes like the Constitution and the IT Act are dense, cross-referenced, and only available in English legalese — and generic chatbots hallucinate fake sections, which is dangerous for legal questions. NyaySaathi answers only from verified source documents, in the user's own language.

details.title: Retrieval engine
bullets: Embedded local Qdrant — no server or Docker needed
Query expansion via a hand-tuned Constitution-to-statute link map (e.g. IT Act 69A → Article 19(2))
Reranking by exact article/section matches, number proximity and keyword overlap
13-language layer: script detection + Hinglish heuristics, English-pivot retrieval, translate-back answers

details.title: Product surfaces
details.body: Three features on one backend: the cited legal chatbot, NyayLens per-document Q&A (isolated collection per upload), and NyayShala — daily auto-generated legal-literacy nuggets across contract, criminal, family, IP, tax and property law.
